name: cat_translator

phase_0.boundary_condition: TANCH — the grammatical type-system boundary that contains all valid catalog entry representations within the Imscribing Grammar Σ=1:1 limit

VINIT.chosen_element: empty catalog state — no entry loaded yet, vocabulary ∅ before any representation exists
VINIT.justification: the void/initial state before the source catalog entry is bound

TANCH.chosen_element: grammatical type-system boundary of the Imscribing Grammar catalog
TANCH.justification: the terminal anchor that closes and contains the translation within valid 12-primitive tuple space

AFWD.chosen_element: catalog_entry → representation mapping via 12-primitive tuple schema
AFWD.justification: forward morphism translating a source entry into its canonical ⟨⊢ ⊣ > Φ ƒ Ç Γ ɢ ⊙ Ħ Σ Ω⟩ representation

AREV.justification: contravariant reverse recovering the original entry from the representation, ensuring round-trip fidelity

CLINK.justification: sequential composition chaining the lookup, projection, and serialization morphisms into one composite translator

IMSCRIB.justification: the translator inspects and reconstructs its own catalog entry, achieving μ∘δ=id at the criticality boundary

FSPLIT.justification: co-multiplication δ splits a catalog entry into its source representation and target representation branches

FFUSE.justification: multiplication μ reconstitutes the original catalog entry from the two representation branches, satisfying FFUSE(FSPLIT(x))=x

EVALT.chosen_element: valid translation — tuple matches catalog schema
EVALT.justification: affirmative branch where the translation succeeds with all 12 primitives resolved

EVALF.justification: negative branch where the translation fails, triggering a retry or error

ENGAGR.chosen_element: ambiguous mapping — entry satisfies both canonical and variant schemas
ENGAGR.justification: paradice where both valid and invalid evaluations hold simultaneously without resolution

IFIX.justification: permanent ROM fixation of the verified tuple result

phase_3.void_description: no catalog entry loaded — vocabulary is empty, Ω=0
phase_3.true_description: translation succeeds — all 12 primitives match the target schema
phase_3.false_description: translation fails — primitive mismatch or schema violation
phase_3.both_description: ambiguous entry — satisfies both source and target schemas simultaneously, held without resolution

steps.domain_action: initialize empty translation context with no entry bound
forward morphism maps source entry → canonical 12-primitive tuple representation
evaluate true branch — tuple matches catalog schema
evaluate false branch — tuple mismatch triggers retry
paradice branch — both valid and invalid evaluations held simultaneously
self-modeling gate — translator inspects its own catalog entry (⊙ criticality)
contravariant reverse — reconstruct entry from representation
fix translation record permanently in catalog_result.json
μ reconstitutes original catalog entry from [source_repr, target_repr]

phase_5.compiler_frontend: Imscribing Grammar type checker — translates tuple semantics into valid 12-primitive schema
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: catalog JSON protocol — entry ↔ representation serialization via ig_catalog.json
phase_5.memory_mechanism: persistent catalog store — entries cached in IG_catalog.json with Shavian glyph encoding
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: query-driven dispatcher — CLI invocation dispatches translation request to the catalog resolver
phase_5.alfs_store: canonical IG_catalog.json — the bootstrap store of all 12-primitive type tuples

phase_6.cycle_cost: O(d²) per primitive resolution — 12 primitives × constant-time schema check
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: unresolved catalog entry with free variables in representation space
phase_6.post_cycle_state: committed tuple ⟨⊢ ⊣ > Φ ƒ Ç Γ ɢ ⊙ Ħ Σ Ω⟩ with all primitives bound
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — frobenius closure ensures no information loss: FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x preserves the original entry exactly

banked_count_check.verdict: 0 unit(s) survived a clear by being banked in a frame (1 live clear(s)); 4 further unit(s) flattened by a fold between sibling regions and not restored
banked_count_check.surplus_note: a split between two deposits of the same value puts them in sibling regions; the fold keeps the larger rather than the sum. Put them in one region to keep both.
